subject.title: Use Codex OAuth auth for ACPX isolated home

question: Should ACPX solve host Codex OAuth by copying complete Codex `auth.json` into the isolated Codex home, or should it preserve the no-auth-copy contract and solve the canonical issue through an explicit-home, setup, or doctor path?
rationale: The patch moves credential-bearing OAuth material across a documented isolation boundary, and related PRs already explore competing shared-home and auth-materialization directions.

options.title: Repair Seeded Auth Before Merge
options.body: Require complete Codex OAuth validation, fallback tests, docs for the new boundary, and redacted live managed ACPX Codex proof before accepting this seeded-auth direction.

options.title: Use The Explicit Home Candidate
options.body: Keep this PR paused or closed and continue the shared-home decision in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/77006.

options.title: Preserve No Auth Copy
options.body: Reject auth-file copying and keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/73910 open for a different setup, doctor, or upstream-supported bridge.

recommendation.title: Repair Seeded Auth Before Merge
recommendation.body: Require complete Codex OAuth validation, fallback tests, docs for the new boundary, and redacted live managed ACPX Codex proof before accepting this seeded-auth direction.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc is the clearest current reviewer for the related Codex-home trust-boundary decision and has recent touches in the affected ACPX files.
